primary_sources.source: GitHub Docs — REST API endpoints for repository contents, Create or update file contents
verified: Updating a file requires the blob SHA of the file being replaced.
GitHub warns that conflicting mutative contents requests must be serialized.

primary_sources.source: GitHub Docs — Best practices for using the REST API / rate limits
verified: GitHub REST API is rate limited and recommends serial requests and stopping/retrying later when rate limited.
These are per-window rate limits rather than a finite monthly/trial compute quota.

exposed_connector_contract: GitHub.update_file requires the current blob SHA for the existing path and returns the resulting commit SHA/content blob SHA.
GitHub.create_file is create-only for a new path and directs replacement through fetch plus update.
The connector explicitly says not to run update/delete writes for the same path in parallel.
exact_chat_repository_evidence.environment_observation: The current invocation successfully fetched the target repository and its exact blobs through the connected GitHub surface; no Work mode, GitHub Actions, Codespaces, package/artifact service, external model/API execution, or manual user action was used for this verification.

supported: A single mutable file can be updated using the currently observed blob SHA as a write precondition, with conflict as an explicit failure mode.
Separate create-only paths can hold PREPARED records without requiring Actions/Codespaces or external compute.
A subsequent exact read can observe the canonical file after a write response is lost, so repository state can serve as recovery evidence.
material_limits: GitHub's documented precondition is the blob SHA of the file being replaced, not a server-enforced semantic owner/generation fence. Monotone owner/generation/sequence validation remains a client protocol obligation.

Blob-SHA compare semantics alone do not exclude an ABA history in which canonical HEAD content is later restored byte-for-byte to an older value. The worker architecture appears to include sequence/revision fields, but the finite model in the source checkpoint does not claim arbitrary out-of-protocol or ABA writes. Therefore the zero-stale-acceptance result must remain limited to protocol-conforming traces with non-reused canonical states.
GitHub documents conflicts/serialization requirements for mutative contents requests; this supports fail-closed retry/checkpoint behavior but is not a multi-object transaction guarantee.
The internal 137257-trace enumeration and evidence hash were not independently reproduced here.

hidden_executor_gate.reason: The route uses the already-exposed repository contents API as transport/state and does not require Work/protected-primary/manual-user execution, Actions, Codespaces, or another hosted executor. incremental_cost_gate.scope_note: No endpoint-specific paid service or quota-bearing compute feature is required for the verified repository-contents operations in the already-connected repository. This is not a universal statement about all GitHub account plans.

Those outcomes still have a residual effect-boundary problem, so the route cannot close the Phase-1 root or any row requiring non-repository side effects.

In particular, do not infer safety under direct out-of-protocol canonical-file rewrites, byte-identical ABA restoration, arbitrary external effects, or cross-service atomicity.
